title: Quotinator Quote Source (extended)
description: Extended object format for curated and user import files. Supports quotes, stage directions, sound cues, and conversation groupings. Backwards-compatible with the flat array format — importers that receive a top-level array treat it as { 'quotes': [...] } with no other sections.

quotes.description: Canonical quote entries. Same schema as source-flat.schema.json.

sources.description: Optional explicit Source declarations (#162) — an author-assigned id decoupling matching from Title/Type/Date content, so all three become correctable. A quote's own 'source' field stays a title string either way; this section is purely additive context a file may also provide.

people.description: Optional explicit Person declarations (#173) — an author-assigned id decoupling matching from Name content, so Name/dateOfBirth/dateOfDeath all become correctable. A quote's own 'author' field stays a name string either way; this section is purely additive context a file may also provide.

characters.description: Optional explicit Character declarations (#175) — an author-assigned id decoupling matching from Name content, so Name becomes correctable; when id is omitted, the entry is matched (or, if genuinely new, created) via ADR 013's Type-anchored, Series-scoped algorithm using name+sourceTitle+sourceType. A quote's own 'character'/'source' fields stay text strings either way; this section is purely additive context a file may also provide.

stageDirections.description: Reusable scene-setting and action descriptions that appear in conversations.

soundCues.description: Reusable audio elements — sound effects, timing cues, ambient sound.

conversations.description: Ordered groupings of quotes, stage directions, and sound cues.

series.description: Optional explicit Series declarations (#180) — a direct continuity of Sources within a Universe. Matched by name only; no explicit id, since the id is generated from the name.

universe.description: Optional explicit Universe declarations (#180) — a fictional world or franchise spanning one or more Series. Matched by name only; no explicit id, since the id is generated from the name.

seasons.description: Optional explicit Season declarations (#375) — an ordered grouping of Sources within a Series. Not television-specific: a magazine's volumes or a podcast's seasons use the same shape. Matched by natural key (seriesName + number) unless an explicit id is given.

source.description: Two shapes. CORRECTION (#162): include 'id' — the Source is matched by that explicit id, so title/type/date can all be corrected. ENRICHMENT (#180): omit 'id' — the Source is matched by natural key (title + type), which makes those two the lookup key rather than correctable values; only 'seriesName' is applied on this path. Omit any property you do not intend to set: a property present with a null value means 'reset this to null', not 'leave it alone'.

id.description: UUID v4, case-insensitive (#180). Optional — omit it to match by natural key (title + type) instead, which is the right shape for a curated overlay file that only enriches Sources this project already generated ids for.

date.description: Publication or release date. Only meaningful alongside an explicit 'id' — a natural-key-matched entry never sets it. Omit entirely unless you intend to set it.

seriesName.description: Name of the Series (#180) this Source belongs to, if any. Resolved to a Series id at import time — never a raw id, matching how a quote's own 'source'/'author' fields are text, not ids. Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

seasonNumber.description: Ordinal of the Season (#375) this Source belongs to, within the Series named by 'seriesName'. A number rather than a name, because a season's ordinal is its natural key within its parent. Resolved to a Season id at import time. Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

series.description: Two shapes (#163). CORRECTION: include 'id' — the Series is matched by that explicit id, so 'name'/'universeName' can both be corrected. CREATION/ENRICHMENT: omit 'id' — the Series is matched, or if genuinely new created, by natural key (name).

id.description: UUID v4, case-insensitive (#163). Optional — omit it to match by natural key (name) instead.

universeName.description: Name of the Universe (#180) this Series belongs to, if any. Resolved to a Universe id at import time, same as Source.seriesName.

season.description: Two shapes (#375). CORRECTION: include 'id' — the Season is matched by that explicit id, so every field can be corrected. CREATION/ENRICHMENT: omit 'id' — the Season is matched, or if genuinely new created, by natural key (seriesName + number). Unlike Series and Universe, the natural key is an ordinal scoped to the parent rather than a globally unique name: 'Season 1' recurs for every series.

id.description: UUID v4, case-insensitive. Optional — omit it to match by natural key (seriesName + number) instead.

number.description: The season's ordinal within its series, and half its natural key.

seriesName.description: Name of the Series this Season belongs to. Resolved to a Series id at import time — never a raw id, same as Source.seriesName.

title.description: The season's own name, where it has one — 'Book One' for Avatar: The Last Airbender's first season. Omit for a season identified by its ordinal alone.

subtitle.description: The season's subtitle, where it has one — 'Water', rendering 'Book One: Water'.

universe.description: Two shapes (#163). CORRECTION: include 'id' — the Universe is matched by that explicit id, so 'name' can be corrected. CREATION/ENRICHMENT: omit 'id' — the Universe is matched, or if genuinely new created, by natural key (name).

id.description: UUID v4, case-insensitive (#163). Optional — omit it to match by natural key (name) instead.

dateOfBirth.description: Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

dateOfDeath.description: Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

character.description: Two shapes (#175). CORRECTION: include 'id' — the Character is matched by that explicit id, so 'name' can be corrected ('sourceType' is immutable once a Character exists — ADR 013 — so 'sourceTitle'/'sourceType' are present for schema consistency but never diffed/written on this path). CREATION/ENRICHMENT: omit 'id' — the Character is matched, or if genuinely new created, via ADR 013's Type-anchored, Series-scoped algorithm using 'name'+'sourceTitle'+'sourceType', the identical identity test a quote's own 'character'/'source' fields resolve through, just decoupled from any specific quote's own text.

id.description: UUID v4, case-insensitive. Optional — omit to match/create via sourceTitle+sourceType+name instead (ADR 013).

sourceTitle.description: The Source this Character is anchored to for ADR 013 matching purposes — same title text a quote's own 'source' field uses. Ignored (never diffed) when 'id' is present.

sourceType.description: The Source.Type anchor (ADR 011) for ADR 013 matching. Ignored (never diffed) when 'id' is present — a Character's Type anchor is immutable once set.

imageUrl.description: Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

soundFileUrl.description: Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

imageUrl.description: Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).

description.description: Omit entirely unless you intend to set it — a present null resets it, an absent property leaves it alone (#190).
